overall.verdict: Low Interaction Risk — Minor Notes Only
overall.summary: You are taking metformin for diabetes and lisinopril for blood pressure. Together they are considered low‑risk, but the combination can sometimes make your blood sugar drop lower than expected. Keep an eye on how you feel and talk to your health‑care team if you notice any changes.

context_advice: As an adult not pregnant, the main concern is the possible extra lowering of blood sugar; regular meals and monitoring can help keep you safe.

drugs.name: lisinopril
drugs.boxed_warning: WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY See full prescribing information for complete boxed warning. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible. ( 5.1 ) Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus. ( 5.1 ) WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY When pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible [see WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS ( 5.1 )] . Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus [see WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS ( 5.1 )] .

label_hits.text: 7.2 Antidiabetics Concomitant administration of lisinopril and antidiabetic medicines (insulins, oral hypoglycemic agents) may cause an increased blood-glucose-lowering effect with risk of hypoglycemia.

explanation.why: Lisinopril can boost the blood‑sugar‑lowering effect of metformin, which may lead to low blood sugar (hypoglycemia).
explanation.timing: Watch for these signs especially when you first start both medicines or if your doses change; ask your doctor about checking your blood sugar regularly.
